description:
The atomic "incremental path, proven against the monolith" commit. Everything introduced here is immediately live (seeded by the seal) and asserted equal to the monolith, so there is no dead-code/unread-fact window — the warnings-as-errors rule is why this lands as one coherent green commit rather than dribbled across unproven intermediates. THIS TICKET IS THE PROOF GATE.

## Change
1. `FactKey::ReturnDemand(ExecutableKey)` (register in ClaimShape::is_cumulative, drive.rs:88, beside ReturnType/ActivationInputs) and `FactKey::RuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey)` (overwrite-fact).
2. `RuntimeDemandMap` — plain single-publisher define-with-changed store for the full `ExecutableRuntimeDemand` (all six fields).
3. `JobEffects.return_demand_contributions: Vec<(ExecutableKey, RuntimeDemand)>` + conclude/extend wiring in world.rs mirroring conclude_/extend_activation_input_contributions (world.rs:588-606); contributions alpha-normalized at the same seam the closure already normalizes demands (define_semantic_closure, world.rs:726).
4. `Job::DeriveRuntimeDemand(ExecutableKey)` + dispatch in jobs/mod.rs. Body REUSES the moved-verbatim transfer functions: assemble a local `demands` map = {E: {return_demand = ReturnDemand(E) fact}} U {callee: {input_demands = RuntimeDemand(callee) fact}}, call `collect_executable_facts` for E and `derive_executable_runtime_demand` unchanged, output `RuntimeDemand(E)`; emit ReturnDemand contributions to callees (the propagate_call_return_demands delivered-demand logic, per-E) and boundary-return contributions for first-class surfaces (the apply_callable_boundary_return_demands rule, per-E); emit latent Executable follow-ups; inherit derive_callable_flow_facts' waits as the job's own waits (so a blocked job EXTENDS its contributions).
5. ReturnDemand base sourcing (the one genuine re-expression of base_return_demand): entry base contributed by SeedRoot (need-based); boundary base contributed by the escape/first-class producer; locally-called base is implicit bottom (callers fill it). No global locally_called set.
6. Seal in SHADOW: for each discovered executable ensure DeriveRuntimeDemand(E) enqueued, wait on RuntimeDemand(E), gather into a shadow map, and `assert_eq!` it against the still-authoritative settle_runtime_demands output before the seal uses the latter.

## Known sharp edge
The easy wrong move is to recreate `locally_called_executables` as a global prepass and use it to decide ReturnDemand bases. That would preserve today's shape mechanically while smuggling the monolithic closure dependency into the new fact path. Do not do that. The current `base_return_demand` decision must be decomposed into monotone contributions: the root entry contributes its need; callers contribute observed delivered-result demand; escape/opaque/first-class boundary evidence contributes boundary demand; absence of callers is not a global fact consulted by `DeriveRuntimeDemand(E)`.

The shadow assertion is the guardrail for this re-expression. If boundary demand for a not-locally-called executable is missing, or a locally-called executable receives boundary demand too early, the gathered map must fail against `settle_runtime_demands` before this ticket can close.

## Why
The agenda becomes the fixpoint (chaotic iteration to the same lfp(F) the monolith reaches by Gauss-Seidel — proposal.html). Shadow keeps the barrier driven by the trusted monolith while exercising the new path corpus-wide; a discrepancy fails AT the demand layer, localized, not five rungs downstream.

## Rip out
Nothing yet — the monolith still authoritative.

## Check
The `assert_eq!` (covering all six ExecutableRuntimeDemand fields incl. callable_flows) holds across `cargo test --lib compiler2_` and `tests/fixture_matrix.rs` — green corpus-wide IS the byte-identical proof. Add a telemetry counter for DeriveRuntimeDemand re-runs vs executables to show the collapse. Add or adjust focused tests around the base-demand re-expression so a global locally-called prepass is unnecessary and caller/boundary contributions are the only source of non-entry ReturnDemand. Zero warnings.
title: Runtime demand: stand up DeriveRuntimeDemand(E) facts behind the seal barrier in shadow mode
